Why does the bold text attribute override the user specified font axes, but if the axes contain italic then they override the text attribute? Shouldn't either both lead to font axes to be overridden or both forcing text attributes to be overridden?

>  Shouldn't either both lead to font axes to be overridden or both forcing text attributes to be overridden?

Yes, thanks for catching that! Was fixing that when I found some kinks, working them out so I've converted this to draft for now

> Shouldn't either both lead to font axes to be overridden or both forcing text attributes to be overridden?

So it turns out that the italic axis and the italic text attribute actually _mean different things_.

Setting the italic text attribute tells dwrite to find the font with italic in its header, whereas setting the italic axis tells dwrite to find the font which has an italic axis of variation with that axis value. Setting the axis can be thought of as setting a restriction on the fonts dwrite will consider. As an example of how this works with Cascadia Code:

Set "ital": 1 - Dwrite gets Cascadia Curve
Text attribute is italic - Dwrite gets Cascadia Curve
Set "ital": 0, text attribute is italic - Dwrite gets Cascadia Code and slants it (it cannot get Cascadia Curve since Cascadia Curve has an italic axis set to 1)

This is the intended way it should work. So in short, the italic axis/attribute should not override each other even though bold does.

Since you changed how italic is handled, please make sure you mention that in the PR body. That body becomes the body of the commit, and it's important that we be able to look at history and learn both the what and the why.

issue_context.title: Setting `wght` axis breaks bold fonts
issue_context.body:
### Windows Terminal version (or Windows build number)

1.11

### Other Software

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

```json
"font": 
{
    "face": "Cascadia Code PL",
    "axes": {
        "wght": 300,
    },
    "size": 14,
}
```

### Expected Behavior

Bold text from SGR 1 should be bold (weight 700).

This sample was made by setting `weight` instead of `axes.wght`:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/189190/127902471-9401b351-93d4-4cf4-8b53-ec0cd2dad16a.png)


### Actual Behavior

It is not bold.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/189190/127902390-7fccb846-c4d5-404c-bffa-7428424a281b.png)

This is impacted by #10852. If the run is considered "simple" (I added `j` to make it complex), bold works fine (but note that the base weight of 300 is lost due to #10852.)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/189190/127902404-6bda537c-b72f-4518-bddf-dc4136fc1e0e.png)
